item.vignette: A 21-year-old woman has recurrent nephrolithiasis and marked hypercalcemia with an elevated parathyroid hormone concentration. Imaging reveals a single parathyroid mass and an ossifying fibroma of the mandible. Her father had parathyroid carcinoma. Germline testing identifies a pathogenic variant in CDC73.
item.lead_in: Loss of which normal protein function most directly promotes tumor formation in this syndrome?

options.A: Calcium sensing by a G-protein-coupled receptor on parathyroid chief cells
options.B: Gs-alpha coupling of the parathyroid hormone receptor to adenylate cyclase
options.C: Nuclear parafibromin tumor-suppressor activity that restrains cell proliferation
options.E: ACTH-dependent cAMP signaling in adrenal zona fasciculata cells

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; requires linking CDC73 to parafibromin and tumor-suppressor biology.
item.tested_construct: CDC73 encodes nuclear parafibromin, a tumor suppressor involved in transcriptional regulation and control of proliferation

explanation.key_explanation: CDC73 encodes parafibromin, a predominantly nuclear protein involved in transcriptional regulation that functions as a tumor suppressor. Loss of functional parafibromin permits uncontrolled proliferation and predisposes to parathyroid tumors in hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome.

distractor_explanations.A: CaSR controls PTH secretion but is not the CDC73 tumor-suppressor product.
distractor_explanations.B: Gs-alpha signaling mediates receptor responses but does not explain CDC73-associated tumor predisposition.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Parafibromin is a nuclear tumor suppressor; loss promotes uncontrolled proliferation.
distractor_explanations.E: ACTH signaling is mediated by MC2R and is unrelated to CDC73.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect CDC73 loss to deficient nuclear parafibromin tumor-suppressor activity in hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome.

evidence_map.claim: CDC73 encodes nuclear parafibromin, a transcription-associated tumor suppressor that restrains proliferation.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains familial parathyroid neoplasia with jaw ossifying fibroma.

item.vignette: A 2-week-old boy has recurrent lethargy and seizures. During an episode, plasma glucose is 28 mg/dL, insulin is inappropriately detectable, beta-hydroxybutyrate is very low, and free fatty acids are suppressed. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic loss-of-function variant in ABCC8, which encodes a subunit of the pancreatic beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channel.
item.lead_in: Which sequence of events most directly causes this infant's hypoglycemia?

options.A: Reduced KATP-channel activity → persistent beta-cell depolarization → voltage-gated calcium-channel opening → insulin release
options.B: Failure of KATP channels to close → beta-cell hyperpolarization → reduced calcium entry → insulin release
options.C: Reduced glucokinase activity → impaired glucose sensing → excessive insulin release at low glucose
options.D: Increased KATP-channel opening → membrane hyperpolarization → increased insulin granule exocytosis
options.E: Reduced insulin-receptor signaling in peripheral tissues → increased insulin secretion despite fasting

explanation.key_explanation: ABCC8 loss can reduce or abolish beta-cell KATP-channel activity. Persistent depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels and drives insulin granule exocytosis even when glucose is low.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct; reduced KATP activity causes persistent depolarization, calcium influx, and inappropriate insulin secretion.
distractor_explanations.B: KATP channels that fail to close reduce insulin secretion and are associated with neonatal diabetes.
distractor_explanations.C: Reduced glucokinase activity raises the glucose threshold for insulin release and causes GCK-MODY hyperglycemia.
distractor_explanations.D: KATP opening hyperpolarizes beta cells and suppresses calcium-dependent insulin release.
distractor_explanations.E: Peripheral insulin resistance does not explain severe neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia from ABCC8 loss.

explanation.educational_objective: Trace congenital hyperinsulinism from loss of beta-cell KATP-channel activity to depolarization, calcium influx, and inappropriate insulin secretion.

evidence_map.claim: ABCC8 encodes a KATP-channel subunit; reduced KATP activity drives inappropriate insulin secretion.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains hypoketotic hypoglycemia with detectable insulin.

evidence_map.claim: KATP channels that do not close appropriately reduce insulin secretion and can cause neonatal diabetes.
Reduced GCK activity impairs glucose sensing and causes mild hyperglycemia.
KATP opening hyperpolarizes beta cells rather than triggering calcium-dependent insulin release.
ABCC8-associated congenital hyperinsulinism is a beta-cell secretion disorder rather than primary peripheral insulin resistance.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Glucose sensing and beta-cell set-point physiology

item.vignette: A 19-year-old woman is found to have a fasting plasma glucose of 124 mg/dL during a routine examination. Prior records show fasting glucose values between 112 and 128 mg/dL since childhood. She has never had ketoacidosis or symptomatic hyperglycemia. Her father and paternal grandmother have similarly mild, stable fasting hyperglycemia. Islet autoantibodies are negative. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in GCK.
item.lead_in: Which physiologic change most directly accounts for this patient's persistent mild hyperglycemia?

options.A: Increased hepatic gluconeogenesis due to constitutive glucagon-receptor signaling
options.B: Failure of pancreatic KATP channels to close despite rising intracellular ATP
options.C: Progressive autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.D: Increased insulin-receptor signaling in skeletal muscle
options.E: A higher glucose concentration is required for beta cells to sense glucose and trigger appropriate insulin secretion

item.tested_construct: Glucokinase as beta-cell glucose sensor in GCK-MODY

explanation.key_explanation: Glucokinase functions as a glucose sensor in pancreatic beta cells. Heterozygous loss of GCK activity shifts the threshold for glucose-stimulated insulin secretion upward, producing lifelong mild stable fasting hyperglycemia.

distractor_explanations.A: Constitutive glucagon signaling is not the inherited defect in GCK-MODY.
distractor_explanations.B: Failure of KATP closure is a different monogenic mechanism and typically produces neonatal diabetes.
distractor_explanations.C: Autoimmune beta-cell destruction is inconsistent with the stable multigenerational phenotype and negative antibodies.
distractor_explanations.D: Increased insulin-receptor signaling would lower plasma glucose.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct; reduced glucokinase activity shifts glucose-stimulated insulin secretion to a higher set point.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize glucokinase as a beta-cell glucose sensor and GCK-MODY as an upward shift in the glucose threshold for insulin secretion.

evidence_map.claim: Glucokinase acts as a beta-cell glucose sensor; GCK loss reduces glucose sensing and insulin release.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains lifelong mild stable fasting hyperglycemia.

evidence_map.claim: KATP channels that fail to close can cause neonatal diabetes with reduced insulin secretion.
MODY is monogenic beta-cell dysfunction rather than autoimmune destruction.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Negative antibodies and family pattern support MODY.

evidence_map.claim: GCK-MODY is caused by reduced glucokinase activity rather than constitutive glucagon signaling.
The lesion impairs glucose sensing rather than increasing peripheral insulin signaling.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Developmental transcriptional regulation of adrenal and gonadal axes

item.vignette: A 15-year-old boy had a salt-wasting adrenal crisis in infancy and has required lifelong glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement. He now has absent pubertal development with low testosterone and inappropriately low gonadotropins. A maternal uncle had a similar history. Genetic testing identifies a hemizygous loss-of-function variant in NR0B1.
item.lead_in: Which normal function of the encoded protein is most directly lost?

options.A: ACTH binding and Gs-mediated cAMP generation at the adrenal cell membrane
options.B: Regulation of gene programs required for development and function of adrenal, hypothalamic-pituitary, and gonadal tissues
options.D: Conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone in all steroidogenic tissues
options.E: Angiotensin II signaling through Gq in zona glomerulosa cells

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; requires integrating X-linked adrenal hypoplasia congenita with DAX1/NR0B1 developmental biology.
item.tested_construct: NR0B1/DAX1 regulates development and function of adrenal and reproductive endocrine tissues

explanation.key_explanation: NR0B1 encodes DAX1, a nuclear regulatory protein important for development and function of the adrenal glands, hypothalamus, pituitary, and gonads. Loss can cause X-linked adrenal hypoplasia congenita with primary adrenal insufficiency and later hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

distractor_explanations.A: ACTH receptor signaling is mediated by MC2R, not NR0B1.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. DAX1 regulates developmental and functional gene programs across adrenal and reproductive endocrine tissues.
distractor_explanations.C: 21-hydroxylase is encoded by CYP21A2 and causes a different form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
distractor_explanations.D: Cholesterol side-chain cleavage is mediated by CYP11A1 rather than DAX1.
distractor_explanations.E: Angiotensin II signaling helps regulate aldosterone but is not the NR0B1 developmental function.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize NR0B1/DAX1 as a developmental regulator of adrenal and hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal tissues in X-linked adrenal hypoplasia congenita.

evidence_map.claim: NR0B1 encodes DAX1, which regulates development and function of adrenal, hypothalamic, pituitary, and gonadal endocrine tissues.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains primary adrenal insufficiency plus hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in an X-linked pedigree.

item.vignette: A 7-month-old infant has poor feeding, vomiting, failure to thrive, hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, and bilateral nephrocalcinosis. Parathyroid hormone is suppressed. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in CYP24A1.
item.lead_in: Which metabolic reaction is most directly impaired in this disorder?

options.C: Vitamin D receptor binding to DNA response elements
options.E: Calcium-sensing receptor activation by extracellular calcium

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; genotype is provided and the item tests the direction of vitamin-D metabolism.
item.tested_construct: CYP24A1 encodes vitamin D 24-hydroxylase that inactivates calcitriol and 25-hydroxyvitamin D

explanation.key_explanation: CYP24A1 encodes 24-hydroxylase, an enzyme that catabolizes active calcitriol and also 25-hydroxyvitamin D. Loss reduces vitamin-D degradation, increasing calcium absorption and causing hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, and nephrocalcinosis.

distractor_explanations.A: Loss of renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase would reduce calcitriol rather than cause vitamin-D-mediated hypercalcemia.
distractor_explanations.B: Hepatic 25-hydroxylation is an activation step upstream of CYP24A1.
distractor_explanations.C: Vitamin-D receptor dysfunction causes resistance to calcitriol rather than impaired catabolism.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. CYP24A1 24-hydroxylase inactivates calcitriol and 25-hydroxyvitamin D.
distractor_explanations.E: CaSR signaling regulates PTH and renal calcium handling but is not the CYP24A1 enzymatic reaction.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize CYP24A1 loss as impaired vitamin-D 24-hydroxylation and catabolism, causing infantile hypercalcemia and nephrocalcinosis.

evidence_map.claim: CYP24A1 encodes 24-hydroxylase, which breaks down calcitriol and 25-hydroxyvitamin D; loss causes hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains suppressed PTH, hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, and nephrocalcinosis.
